en: The Hymn to the Auspicious Shower of Gold (Śrīkanakadhārāstotra)

May the playful sidelong glance of the auspicious goddess bestow blessings upon me—she who takes refuge in the limb of Hari adorned with horripilation, just as a female bee resorts to a tamāla tree adorned with buds; she who has accepted all sovereign splendor. || 1 ||

May she who was born from the ocean grant me the splendor of Lakṣmī— she who, like a female bee upon a great blue lotus, repeatedly moved back and forth across the eyes of Murāri as she, in her innocence, offered expressions of love and bashfulness to his face.
May the eyes of the Consort of the Serpent-Lord, which have approached Mukunda— the root of bliss and the master of the bodiless god of love— with joy as he closes his eyes,
and whose eyelashes and pupils remain half-closed in a sidelong glance, lead to my prosperity.

May that garland of side-glances from the lotus-dwelling Lakṣmī—which shines like a necklace of sapphires upon the chest of the Conqueror of Madhu, who wears the Kaustubha gem—bestow auspiciousness upon me; for even the Lord’s own glance bestows all desires. || 4 ||

May the daughter of Bhārgava, whose venerable form is the mother of all worlds, grant me auspicious blessings—she who, like lightning upon a rain-cloud, flashes upon the chest of Kaiṭabhāri as he is embraced by the garland of dark clouds. || 5 ||

Indeed, by the power of that very state which was first attained by me, may the slow and languid half-glance of the Daughter of the Ocean fall here upon Madhumathin, who is now the possessor of auspiciousness through Manmatha.
May that half-glance of Indirā, which is capable of bestowing the splendor of the station of the Lord of All Gods, which is the cause of supreme bliss even for the Enemy of Mura,
and which resembles the interior of a blue lotus, rest upon me for a moment.

May the gaze of her who has the lotus as her seat—whose light is like the interior of a blossoming lotus, and by which even those whose minds are distinguished by their desires easily attain the station of heaven—grant me the nourishment I desire. 8.

May the rain-cloud of the eyes of Nārāyaṇa’s beloved consort, having long since dispelled the nature of evil deeds, bestow a stream of wealth upon this dejected young bird who possesses nothing, like a wind-fanned breeze.

Salutations to her, the youthful one, the sole teacher of the three worlds, who is established in the playful acts of creation, maintenance, and dissolution— she who is known as Gīrdevatā, Garuḍadhvajasundarī, Śākambharī, and the beloved of the moon-crested Lord.
Salutations to Śruti, the source of the fruits of auspicious deeds; salutations to Rati, an ocean of delightful qualities;
salutations to Śakti, whose abode is the hundred-petaled lotus; salutations to Puṣṭi, the beloved of Puruṣottama. || 11 ||
Homage be to her whose face resembles a lotus; homage be to her who is the source of prosperity born from the ocean of milk;
homage be to her who is like the nectar of the moon; homage be to her who is the beloved of Nārāyaṇa.
Salutations to her whose throne is a golden lotus; salutations to the sovereign of the circle of the earth;
salutations to her who is intent on compassion for the gods and others; salutations to the beloved of the one whose weapon is the Śārṅga bow. || 13 ||

Salutations be to the Goddess, the delight of the Bhrigus; salutations be to her who dwells upon the chest of Viṣṇu. Salutations be to Lakṣmī, whose abode is the lotus; salutations be to the beloved of Dāmodara. || 14 ||
Homage be to Her of radiant beauty, whose eyes are like lotuses; homage be to Prosperity, the source of the worlds!
Homage be to Her worshipped by gods and others; homage be to Her, the beloved of Nanda’s son! 15.

O lotus-eyed Mother, may my prostrations—which bring about prosperity, delight all the senses, possess the power to bestow imperial sovereignty, and are intent upon uprooting evil—constantly attend to me alone; I pray, do not disregard me. 16.
I worship you, the mistress of the heart of Murāri, whose ritual of worship through a sidelong glance bestows all wealth and success upon your servant by means of [your] speech, limbs, and mind. 17.
O Goddess dwelling in the lotus, holding a lotus in your hand, resplendent with white garments, perfumes, and garlands;
O Blessed One, beloved of Hari, charming one who bestows prosperity upon the three worlds, be gracious unto me! 18.

In the morning, I bow to the Mother of the worlds, the consort of the Lord of all realms, the daughter of the nectar-ocean, whose limbs are bathed in the pure and beautiful waters of the celestial river poured from the mouths of golden jars by the long-armed [gods]. 19.
O Lotus, beloved of the lotus-eyed one, look upon me with side-glances rippling with a flood of compassion; for I am among those who possess nothing, the foremost vessel for unfeigned mercy. (20)
O Goddess, be gracious, O Sovereign of the Universe, Mother of the World, whose limbs are auspicious, O Lotus-eyed One, O Life-giver!
Look upon me daily with compassionate side-glances, for I am one who has come to you for refuge, my heart terrified by poverty. (21)
Those who daily praise with these hymns Ramā, the mother of the three worlds who consists of the three Vedas,
become superior in virtue and partakers of most exalted fortune on this earth, their hearts purified by the wise.
Thus ends the Śrī Kanakadhārā Stotra composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
